official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 plan-making guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG published a new practical guide to creating a neighbourhood plan on 31 March 2026, covering designation, evidence, consultation, examination, referendum and making the plan.

official_measurement_examples.name: Basic conditions gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: A draft neighbourhood plan must meet statutory basic conditions and other legal requirements before it can proceed through examination and referendum.

official_measurement_examples.name: Made-plan status
official_measurement_examples.fact: A neighbourhood plan becomes part of the statutory development plan when it is formally made; a draft or consultation document is not equivalent to a made plan.

official_measurement_examples.name: Referendum distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A successful referendum is an important statutory stage but is not itself an individual parcel planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Modification routes
official_measurement_examples.fact: Neighbourhood-plan modifications can follow different procedures depending on whether they materially change the nature of the plan, including cases where a new referendum is not required.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 toolkit warning
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some 2026 neighbourhood-planning toolkits expressly say they remain useful background but may not yet reflect recent policy changes, so toolkit publication date is not proof that every policy statement is current.

official_measurement_examples.name: Policy versus permission
official_measurement_examples.fact: A neighbourhood-plan allocation or policy can influence development decisions but does not by itself establish title, site access, infrastructure capacity or an implementable planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Development-plan context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Neighbourhood policies operate alongside strategic policies and other material considerations; they must not be read as a standalone parcel yield calculation.

core_rules: draft neighbourhood plan is not a made plan
area designation is not planning permission
forum designation is not planning permission
basic-conditions compliance is not parcel approval
examination recommendation is not a made plan
referendum result is not individual planning permission
made neighbourhood plan is development-plan policy not land title
policy toolkit date is not automatic policy currency
modification route must retain referendum context
strategic and neighbourhood policies must retain hierarchy/context
no parcel neighbourhood-policy clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG/GOV.UK and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. March-July 2026 neighbourhood-planning guidance was retained with designation, basic-condition, examination, referendum, made-plan and policy-lineage distinctions; no parcel promotion.
